sentences.text: Cryptarcus is a large, four-legged plant-eating ceratopsid dinosaur from the middle Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous found in Alberta.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a skull measuring approximately 94 centimeters in length, and its frill is about 120% of the length of the rest of the skull.
This skull is distinguished by a deep embayment on the back of the parietal frill and dome-shaped ornamentation along the edge of this embayment, while each squamosal bone bears eight episquamosals.
The species was first described in 1940 by Charles Mortram Sternberg as Chasmosaurus russelli.

A 2026 study by Holmes, Mallon, Ryan, and Evans reprepared the holotype to clarify anatomy obscured by plaster reconstruction and formally established the genus Cryptarcus in the Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences.
The partial parietal TMP 2013.019.0038 was recognized as belonging to the species in addition to the holotype, with fossils found in the Dinosaur Park Formation in Canada.
Cryptarcus is a chasmosaurine ceratopsid that was established as a new genus for Chasmosaurus russelli.

Taxonomic revisions found that the holotype cannot be definitively resolved as closer to either Chasmosaurus or Pentaceratops, with alternative methods supporting both possibilities. A 2026 reassessment by Holmes and colleagues produced phylogenetic results based on iterations with and without weighting, yielding conflicting results where some iterations place Cryptarcus closer to Pentaceratops and others closer to Chasmosaurus.
Cryptarcus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) period, and its type locality is the Dinosaur Park Formation in the region of Alberta.

It was previously debated that Chasmosaurus russelli came from lower layers of the Dinosaur Park Formation while C. belli came from upper layers, but this was later challenged after the rediscovery of the holotype quarry revealed it to be from a high layer.
In 2010, Nick Longrich argued that many specimens referred to C. russelli represented Mojoceratops perifania, but this view was rejected by most researchers.
Researchers noted that definitive classification of chasmosaurs is difficult and that Cryptarcus might later be associated with another genus due to the lack of a definite link to Chasmosaurus.
Recent hypotheses suggesting an evolutionary trend from Cryptarcus russelli through Pentaceratops to produce Terminocavus are not supported by the phylogenetic analysis presented in this study.
